October 2011 # Mind the scrap - Scrap availability has tightened as merchants hold back material for which they paid more than they can receive if they sell it, which will support cathode demand. This will become more acute China, as scrap on the water arrives and is held. - Strikes continue to plague the miners, as do disruptions from ore grade declines and resource nationalism, which is constraining refined output. The dearth of scrap in China could also see a reduction in refined production that will support cathode demand. - Copper demand is not doing badly, and there are no specific signs the crisis in confidence has yet affected physical copper consumption. However, consumers are being cautious and the price will be volatile over the next month, as direction will be driven by developments in the resolution of the Eurozone debacle. |The supply/demand

The dithering has now meant that markets have lost confidence in the currency union. As we stated in the special update from our Price Risk Management colleagues, some inves

tors have sold copper. CRU believes that the bulk of the flight was by investors with short term horizons, such as the CTAs (Commodity Investment Advisors) and some hedge funds. Some longer term investors may also have sold copper. Given the extent of the reversal in sentiment, we estimate that the CTAs have now gone short on copper. The chart on the right supports this view, as it shows the sharp swing in the net position of non-commercial market participants on Comex from a large net long to a net short position for the first time in almost two years. ### Net position goes short for the first time since Oct 2009 Comex futures & options, Jan ‘09 – Sep ‘11 ‘000 lots

## **Demand slowing in Western Europe and USA** The sell off across commodity markets is due to fears over what might happen should the Eurozone fail to address its governance issues. Macroeconomic indicators show that there has been a slowing in the rate of growth recently, but no sharp deceleration – yet. Recent metal market PMIs from Markit show the US copper market is reported to be the softest, Europe flat to modestly up and Asia growing modestly. This is mirrored by reports from our contacts at semi fabricators and from other copper market players, who also confirm that consumers are mainly feeding their requirements for cathode from contracted material. So far, there are no specific signs that macroeconomic and financial issues in the industrialised countries have yet affected physical copper consumption. We estimate that global refined copper consumption in Q3 grew by an estimated 1.8% y- o-y and will register 3.0% for 2011. Quarterly growth rates are slowing, in part due to comparisons with the peak period of the recovery in 2010. ## **Domestic demand increasingly important in China and emerging markets** In China, the broader manufacturing PMI showed an overall decline in output in September for the third consecutive month. This is in response to the credit tightening measures that the central bank has been employing to rein in inflation. Copper demand has been affected by the broader slow down. We estimate that refined consumption growth in China slowed in Q3 to 3.4% y-o-y from 5.7% in Q2 and we expect consumption growth q-o-q in Q4 to be flat. Cathode imports had averaged below the 200,000t/m level that is necessary to meet the structural shortfall in the Chinese cathode market from February to July this year, as stocks that had been built up over the past two years were run down. However, refined imports surged by 21% m-o-m to 235,500t in August, while exports fell by 88% m-o-m to just 500t. Net imports were therefore 235,000t in August, making this the highest month so far in 2011. Earlier in the year, we estimate that almost 25

0,000t of the around 550,000t of stock in bonded warehouses was used as collateral for financing deals.  The subsequent efforts of the authorities to stamp out the use of cathode imports as a financing mechanism appear to be bearing fruit, as we believe the stocks held in such deals have largely been sold.  We estimate that there are now only 250,000t of cathode in Shanghai bonded warehouses, with most of this being trader working inventory.  Consumer stock levels also remain low due to the tight credit availability in the country. Therefore, we expect to see Chinese cathode imports pick up to average at least 200,000t/m in Q4, mostly to meet contractual commitments and trader requirements.

Copper consumption in other emerging markets, particularly the other BRIC countries and the rest of Asia, are showing mixed results.  Consumption growth is variable across the MENA region due to the effects of the Arab Spring, while in Southeast Asia we forecast 6.2% growth for 2011 as a whole.  Central and Eastern Europe is one of the star performing regions, on course for over 16% refined consumption growth this year. The relatively strong performance of the emerging markets is mainly being driven by domestic demand, as the process of “decoupling” from export led growth (or at least exports to industrialised countries) continues.  This is a natural consequence of the industrialisation process, which was accelerated by the 2008-09 recession having mainly affected industrialised countries.  Russia, for example, is seeing strong growth in domestic consumption of copper for wirerod to feed both domestic wire & cable manufacturers but also for export.  The latter have doubled following the re-imposition of the export tariff on copper cathode earlier this year.  As a result, some markets are seeing a rise in Russian imports, including the USA, Turkey and some Western European countries.  Not surprisingly, these imports are weighing negatively on already soft refined consumption prospects, particularly in the USA. 

## **Political feebleness breeds uncertainty** 

Copper demand is not doing badly.  However, the dismal political leadership being shown in the Eurozone (and to a lesser extent the USA) in addressing the high and rising levels of sovereign debt is leaving the market unable to confidently judge volumes for annual cathode contracts in 2012.  With the mating season kicking off at LME Week, the negotiations are likely to take longer this year and may extend well into next year, as was the case during the downturn in 2008.  However, in terms of the price, the fundamentals of the copper market in the next year support our view that, barring any slump into deep recession, levels around $7,000-8,000/t is a fair price for copper, as reflected by the forward curve.  The key factors that should support copper prices are the continuing “decoupling”

of emerging markets from dependence on the industrialised world (as already mentioned above), scrap market dynamics and the chronically low growth in mine supply. 

## **Scrap dynamics should support cathode demand – if the worst happens...** 

When looking at the copper market one has to look at the total consumption of copper by semi fabricators, both refined and scrap.  When scrap availability declines, this tends to boost cathode demand to meet the resulting gap in copper units that were being supplied by scrap.  As proven during the downturn in 2008 and 2009, this scrap dynamic can have a significant effect on the cathode market.  So far this year the scrap impact has been negative on refined consumption.  Consumers that can take scrap have been doing so and selling back to the market some of the cathode bought on contract that became surplus to requirements.  Quantities, though, have been modest and therefore have not been enough to weigh significantly on premia. 

There are indications that scrap discounts narrowed after the price collapsed, due to scrap dealers holding back material to avoid incurring losses on scrap bought when copper prices were over $1,000/t higher.  In China, discounts fell over the past month in response to supply falling more than demand, with the discount for No.1 scrap in recent weeks actually turning into a premium.  Chinese scrap merchants had increased their buying in the USA prior to the price plummeting, which also put pressure on US discounts.  What is different in China now from 3 years ago is that the reneging on scrap contracts in late 2008 and early 2009 means Chinese scrap merchants have to pay up front for imported scrap.  This means the price exposure has been transferred to China.  Therefore, no matter what happens in the Eurozone, we expect to see a further tightening of scrap availability in China.  “Expensive” scrap bought recently will arrive over the coming weeks.  Chinese scrap merchants will likely hold it back from the market to avoid losses, which we anticipate will be positive for cathode demand.  The boost to cathode could also come from reduced refined production, as secondary smelters are likely to see a lack of raw materials which would lead to lower output. 

## **...as will chronic mine output constraints...** 

The first half of 2011 saw disruptions to mine output of 200,000t more than we had been expecting in our forecasts for the year in our January Quarterly, due to lower ore grades, strikes and weather.  The mines

continue to face such disruptions.  At the moment, Freeport’s Grasberg mine is on strike and there is the threat of a strike at its Cerro Verde mine in Peru.  In Canada, workers have also recently voted to strike at Teck’s Highland Valley as negotiations, ahead of their labour contract expiring on 30th September, have not been successful to date.  In add

ition, Mongolia looking to renegotiate the terms of Oyu Tolgoi could be a sign of an increase in resource nationalism.  The slow growth in mine output has led to a tighter concentrates market. TC/RCs have dropped below $50/t and 5¢/lb, reflecting a deficit market which is constraining growth in refined output. 

## **...and stocks are not excessive** 

The market turmoil and demand uncertainty is resulting in a pull back by some consumers to commit to buy spot cathode.  However, given relatively low consumer stock levels, this is not quite the downside threat to the price that it would have been in years past.  Furthermore, as noted above, we believe that the excess inventory in China has largely been run down to feed the deficit that had accrued there in Q1-Q3.  Given the low stocks elsewhere in the supply chain, we do not see world exchange stocks of 650,000t by the end of Q3 as excessive. 

Chilean miners have been offering small quantities of spare material in a spot tender basis.  Enami tendered 500t of material to be shipped in October, which was awarded at a premium of $117/t M+1 cif Rotterdam and went to China.  We understand a Pucobre tender for 1,200t of grade A cathode was sold with shipments scheduled for Q4 2011, though we have yet to confirm the terms.  In addition, there was a tender of material from Las Cenizas.  The first lot was of 250t non-LME registered grade A cathode and the second 100t of standard cathode for shipment in October.  We heard that this tender was awarded with premiums of $80/t for the first lot and $50-60/t for the second one, both with cif Rotterdam parity.  Finally, we are aware of miners easily selling small extra lots of copper to Asian buyers on a private basis. 

## **Premia down in US and Europe, but head higher in China** 

Following the decline in the price, we would expect to see an increase in imports into China, especially given the positive arbitrage with the LME.  The spot premium also showed an upward trend in September rising in the month from nearer $100/t at the start of the month towards $140/t by the end.  Given that the collateral financing deals have been drying up, we believe that the increase in spot premia is being driven by actual consumers and traders.  The expected tightening of the scrap market and continuation of the positive LME arbitrage will likely lead to premia remaining at or possibly rising from the elevated levels hit recently. 

The European market is very cautious as fears of a financial crisis increase.  Consumers that are in the market are buying for immediate requirements only and only in small quantities.  As a result, copper premiums are down to US$40-70/t from the US$60-90/t seen during the summer, with some consumers still selling excess material on the spot market.  The Mediterranean is facing more difficulties, as they tend to export rod to North Africa, where wire & cable production has been hit by geopolitical events.  There have also been reports of some cust

omers postponing deliveries, but the larger consumers in the region have been quick to deny they are doing so. In the US, the spot market is reported to be as quiet as it has been throughout the year, given that enough quantities were locked in the annual contracts. Freight rates remain high and are affecting spot cathode market premiums. The lack of activity has finally hit premiums, which declined to 4.0-5.5¢/lb after a sustained period from June-August in a 5.0-6.0¢/lb range. ## **Prices to gyrate** Until there is some clarity on the fate of the Eurozone, financial and commodity markets including copper will face volatile sentiment. We therefore expect to see the copper price trade in a wide range over the next month, driven by investors’ reactions to developments in the Eurozone. At the moment downside support is being tested at $7,150/t, with $6,500/t the next target. The facility constituted one of two of the company’s North American copper tube mills, with the other plant located in Fulton, MS. The affected operation housed equipment for the manufacture of copper tube, line sets and PVC drainage, waste and vent fittings. No one was injured in the incident, however, the extent of the damage to the building was very severe and just over a third of the plant’s workforce has since been laid-off. The company’s North American operations serve the HVAC, plumbing and refrigeration markets and as such have been meeting weak demand. The already shrinking US construction sector contracted 15.6% y-o-y in 2009, declined again by 3.7% y-o-y in 2010 and we estimate it to have fallen 2% y-o-y in H1 2011. It therefore comes as no surprise that Mueller’s North American copper tube mills were running below full capacity ulitisation prior to the incident on 6th September. In fact, the company does not expect to have any problems fulfilling orders from its plant in Fulton. Mueller’s Q2 2011 results attributed 13.8% or US$90M of its net sales revenue to rising material costs, such as copper cathode, however, the company also capitalised on widened copper scrap discounts during spring and early summer via the use of its electric arc furnace at Wynne. With the closure of the Wynne plant, the company will only be able to process a modest amount of scrap in the production of copper tube as the Fulton facility uses a shaft furnace which primarily melts copper cathode and internal mill scrap. In last month’s issue we reported that Mueller made an expression of interest in acquiring unnamed assets in Reading, PA owned by Industrias Unidas SA de CV and its subsidiary, United Copper Industries Inc. (UCI). At the time of writing, the company is

understood to be continuing discussions. 

## **Copper plate, sheet, strip and foil (Cu PSSF) & copper alloy plate, sheet, strip and foil (CuAL PSSF) trends** 

Globally, Cu PSSF production and consumption contracted by 5.6% and 6.1% y-o-y in Q2 2011, which represents a weakening in the performance of the industry since the near zero year-on-year growth seen in Q1.  This is attributed to a number of reasons: a decline in the rate of growth for Q1 and Q2 2011 which is measured against a particularly strong recovery in H1 2010 that saw the market grow by around 30% y- o-y.  Also weaker than expected demand in most regions caused by sustained high copper prices and macroeconomic uncertainty; but also, importantly, a lower than expected Q2 uptick in Chinese demand due to the effect of continuing monetary tightening, reducing Chinese semi-fabricators utilisation rates. The CuAL PSSF segment performed slightly less weakly as global production contracted by 2.2% and consumption declined by 1.8% y-o-y in Q2.  The causes for this trend are largely the same as those attributed to the shrinkage seen in the Cu PSSF market with the exception that the CuAL PSSF market encountered significant positive growth in China as we suspect it took share from pure copper PSSF. 

In the first half of 2011, China remained the most important country for both the copper PSSF and copper alloy PSSF product segments.  China’s share of worldwide production grew from 31.6% and 36.1% in H2 2010 to reach 32.4% and 39.9% for Cu PSSF and CuAL PSSF respectively in H2 2011.  Demand for both products is also strongest in China as it accounted for 43.0% and 47.1% of global consumption in H1.

While the level of Chinese copper and copper alloy PSSF consumption exceeded production in H1 2011 by an estimated 112,000t and 80,000t, respectively, causing the production deficit to narrow by 7.1%  and 7.5% y-o-y.  This indicates that China is becoming less dependent on international trade as its production capacity has been growing faster than demand. 

There were numerous reports on new flat rolled copper production capacity in China in H1 2011. Chinalco Luoyang Co. Ltd. successfully installed 105,000t/y of new copper strip and plate capacity, bringing its total capacity to 210,000t/y.  The new production line has been ramping up output since March and the company plans to produce 160,000 to 170,000t in 2011, an increase of 18% y-o-y. Chinalco Luoyang also commenced production at a new 20,000t/y copper and copper alloy sheet rolling line in Henan province in July.  Henan Sanfeng Copper Industry Company Limited started production at its first phase 50,000t/y capacity expansion project for copper sheet and strip in August, the overall project capacity is anticipated to rise to 100,000t/y once fully open.  Tianjin Chuangxinyuan Investment Co. Ltd. will also trial production at its n

ew copper strip and foil fabricating facitility in Tianjin in October. Once completed the operation is expected to have a capacity of 10,000t/y. In addition to this, Nanya Copper Foil Co. Ltd. has invested in a new 11,900t/y copper foil plant, which will begin construction in September. With this new facility, Nanya is expected to have the largest combined copper foil production capacity in China. It was also reported that Anhui Jincheng Copper Share Co. Ltd. will commission its 30,000t/y copper sheet and strip mill in the end of December, which is later than originally planned because of the design revision to develop an extra 10,000t/y capacity. ## **China exhibits growth in copper alloy PSSF sector as substitution between product segments takes place** Demand for CuAL PSSF in China grew considerably compared to the growth of its pure copper counterpart. In H1 2011, CuAL PSSF consumption in China grew by 4.9% y-o-y, whereas pure copper PSSF demand fell by 2.2% y-o-y. Changes in production of these segments is generally driven by the same trend in the electrical /electronic interconnect market. It is understood that end-use substitution from pure copper flat rolled products to alloyed flat rolled products, driven by high copper prices is occurring in the Chinese market. In essence this reduces the copper intensity, replacing copper to some extent with a cheaper metal such as zinc, and therefore lowering the cost of items containing flat rolled copper products. However, a drop in the electrical conductivity of the resulting items is a repercussion of the substitution. This means that areas such as the infotech sector, which demand copper flat rolled products for the manufacture of high performance goods such as laptops, mobile devices etc. are not likely to replace a pure copper flat rolled product with an inferior alloyed counterpart, despite the cost benefit. We believe that this inter-material substitution has been occurring more aggressively in less immune sectors, which can be characterised as manufacturing relatively low value-added products (encouraging cost reduction) with less than a critically high emphasis on electrical performance. The consumer and general products (25% of global Cu PSSF usage in 2009), transportation (7% of global Cu PSSF usage in 2009) and air conditioning and refrigeration (2% of global Cu PSSF usage in 2009), are examples of such areas. # Industry News ## **Consumption** - A fire broke out at **Mueller Industries** ’ **Wynne** factory on 6th September, severely damaging a building which houses the facility’s casting operations for copper tube production, as well as the manufacturing of PVC fittings and fabrication of line sets for air conditioning applications. Noone was injured in the fire, however, 170 of the plant’s 465 employees have been laid off. - **Hussey Copper Ltd.** , the Philadelphia-based copper semis fabricator, is rumoured to be up for sale. The company has recently been struggling to finance elevated input costs, attributed to high copper prices. In a bid to alleviate cash-flow issues stemming from the higher cost of financing, Hussey firstly reduced its payment terms in January from a 45-day to a 30-day basis. Two months later, the company asked customers to pay for freight charges on orders, which mills’ traditionally absorbed into their own costs. Hussey manufactures copper and copper alloy rolled products, rods and electrical bar at two operations located in **Leetsdale** , PA and **Eminence** , KY. - China headquartered, **Golden Dragon Precise Copper Tube Group Inc.** has not yet broken ground at its proposed USD$100M copper pipe and tube plant in **Thomasville** , Alabama. The company was © 2011 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 13 of 16 October 2011 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com - expected to begin construction of its first U.S. semis fabricating operation between July and August. The facility will supply 100Mlbs/y of products to the heating, ventilation and air conditioning sector. - **Sindicel** , the Brazilian electric conductors and non-ferrous metals association, expects sales of copper and copper alloy wire, cable and semis to rise by 10% y-o-y in 2011. Domestic production is also predicted to increase by 10% y-o-y in the same period. The sector’s output and sales have been boosted by demand from the automotive, construction and telecommunications industries. Increased demand from China has also been cited as a principal factor. In addition, a poll of Brazilian copper products producers revealed that half were operating above an 80% capacity utilisation. **Ibram** , the national mining association, also reported that wire and cable production will grow by 39% by 2016. This will be primarily driven by the construction industry due to events such as the 2014 World Cup, the 2016 Olympics and also government programs. According to Ibram, Brazilian output of co

pper products was 230,000t in 2010 and is anticipated to grow to 475,000t by 2014. 

- **Aurubis AG** , the Germany head-quartered refined copper and copper products fabricator, expressed its interest in pursuing additional acquisitions overseas after recently completing its takeover of **Luvata** ’s Rolled Products Division.  Aurubis has been interested in companies which operate overseas, primarily in South America, but has so far failed to identify any likely candidates. 

- **Luvata** , a major global copper semis fabricator, announced that it expects a 10% rise in sales in 2011 on the back of strong Asian demand.  The company expects sales of around 335,500t of copper semis this year, in comparison to 305,000t in 2010.  In 2010, Luvata achieved sales growth of 19.6% y-o-y. The company believes that copper demand is recovering well, with robust growth in China and South East Asia, where the residential construction, manufacturing and electrical engineering sectors are performing strongly. 

- **Leoni AG** , a leading automotive wiring harness provider, announced on 5<sup>th</sup> September that an agreement has been reached to acquire the outstanding 50% of its joint venture partner, **Daekyeung T&G** , effective on 1st January 2012.  Leoni acquired 50% of Daekyeung in June 2008 after an agreement one year earlier to cooperate on wiring harness development.  Daekyeung produces wiring harnesses for the automotive industry in three facilities located in China.  The South Korean company is expected to generate sales between €130M - €140M in 2012 and will help Leoni’s objective to double sales revenue in South Korea by 2015. 

- The **Japan Copper and Brass Association** reported that production of rolled copper products fell by 5.3% y-o-y to 70,670t in August, the biggest fall this year.  The decline is linked to weak demand for silicon chips , connectors and automobiles .  Previously, the association reported that total production of copper and copper alloy semis fell by 4.1% y-o-y to 72,770t in July. 

- China’s **Customs General Administration** reported that imports of refined copper declined by 11.9% y-o-y in August 2011 to 235,509t.  August imports of copper concentrate, on the other hand, increased by 42.1% y-o-y to 675,928t.  Copper scrap saw a y-o-y decline of 4.0% in August. 

- It was reported on 9<sup>th</sup> September that **Tianjin Chuangxinyuan Investment Co. Ltd.** plan to invest RMB613M in the development of a 10,000t/y high-precision copper strip and foil project in Tianjin. Trial production will take place in October of this year, following the installation of two production lines with a combined capacity of 2400t/y.  Tianjin Chuangxinyuan Investment will become China's biggest producer of copper strip and foil upon the project's completion.

(Workers earlier staged an 8-day walkout that ended on 11<sup>th</sup> July.)  The strike is ongoing at the time of writing (28<sup>th</sup> September) and there have been no reports

The 8-day strike in July at the mine cost the company 16,000t of contained copper in lost production.  Prior to the 15<sup>th</sup> September strike, Grasberg was expected to produce 493,000t of copper-in-concentrates in 2011. 















- On 7<sup>th</sup> September, workers at a **Freeport-McMoRan** majority-owned mine, **Cerro Verde** in Peru, took part in a 48-hour cautionary strike, demanding wage increases and better working conditions as part of their new 38-month labour contracts, which were due for renewal on 31<sup>st</sup> August 2011. Workers subsequently staged another strike on 14<sup>th</sup> September, however, it ended on 17th September after the strike was declared illegal by the government and violent clashes involving the police occurred, which led to several protester injuries.  The workers’ union at Cerro Verde threatened to stage another strike on 28<sup>th</sup> September, which was set to last for an indefinite period of time.  However, this strike was later postponed for a day while talks continued.  Cerro Verde had been expected to produce around 317,000t of contained copper in 2011. 

- Mining in Northern Chile was disrupted by a 3-hour blackout which took place at 20:30 on 25<sup>th</sup> September in the area extending from Copiapo to the El Maule region. **Antofagasta** ’s **Los Pelambres** mine, **Anglo American** ’s **Los Bronces** mine and **Codelco** ’s **Andina** and **El Teniente** mines were all paralysed by the power cut, with production taking place at minimum capacity under energy supply from back-up generators.   The **Collahuasi** and **Chuquicamata** mines were not affected by the blackout. 

- **Southern Copper Corporation** is under threat of losing the water licence for two of its operations in Peru.   The threat comes as a result of local governing bodies putting pressure on the central government to cut water supply to the mines in response to the alleged pollution they cause.   The operations under threat include the 145,000t **Cuajone** mine and the 160,000t **Toquepala** mine. 

- The recently elected Peruvian government approved a new system for royalty payments in the mining sector on 22<sup>nd</sup> September that aims to raise funds of PEN3.0B (US$1.1B) per year.  In addition to a special mining income tax, the new legislation requires that those mining companies without tax stability agreements pay between 1% and 12% of their operating profits (a change from 1% to 3% of their net sales).  Mining companies with ta

x stability agreements will pay tax as outlined by the agreement but will also owe 4% to 13.12% royalty rates on operating profits.  Mining companies in Peru currently pay 30% income tax as well as royalties.  The purpose of the tax stability agreements is to protect projects from changes to taxes imposed by future governments. 

- A strike that was due to take place on 2<sup>nd</sup> September was averted at Chile’s **Collahuasi** mine after workers accepted a bonus adjustment and a one-off goodwill payment offer from the mine’s management.  The strike threat came as a result of workers demanding better benefits and an end to alleged anti-union measures.  The unrest follows on shortly from a 24-hour strike at the mine that took place on 31<sup>st</sup> July 2011.  In 2011, Collahuasi is expected to produce around 505,000t of copper-inconcentrate and 35,000t of EW cathode. 

- On 27<sup>th</sup> September, 99.5% of unionised workers at **Teck** ’s **Highland Valley** mine in Canada voted in favour of going on strike if the union’s demands are not met in the ongoing contract negotiations with the company.  The labour contract is due to expire on 30<sup>th</sup> September.  Production of copper-inconcentrates at Highland Valley is expected to be 95,000t in 2011. 

- **Rio Tinto** and **Anglo American** announced plans on 5<sup>th</sup> September to divest their shareholding in the **Palabora Mining Company** .  Rio Tinto and Anglo American hold shares of 57.7% and 16.8% respectively in Palabora.  Both companies intend to sell their shareholdings through a joint commercial process.  The key asset of Palabora is a large block cave copper mine and smelter complex in South Africa.

## **Exploration and Development** 





- Reports emerged on 25<sup>th</sup> September that the Mongolian government is looking at a proposed revision of the 2009 deal on the **Oyu Tolgoi** copper and gold project.  The deal gave **Ivanhoe Mines** (and its major shareholder **Rio Tinto** ) a 66% share of the project, leaving the Mongolian government with the remaining 34% shareholding. However, on 7<sup>th</sup> September, a group of 20 lawmakers submitted a letter to the prime minister demanding that the nation’s stake in Oyu Tolgoi be raised to 50% in the light of Ivanhoe’s recent high profits.  In other news, Rio Tinto, on 27<sup>th</sup> September, increased its stake in Ivanhoe by 0.5% for US$73M, bringing its total ownership up to 49% of the company and equalling the ownership limit which both companies agreed on in December 2010.  Terms for Rio Tinto’s increased shareholding are reported to involve ceasing arbitration against Ivanhoe and also taking operating control of the project. 

- **Gecamines** , the DR Congo’s state-owned mining company, said on 17<sup>th</sup> September that it would audit all of its joint ventures with international companies

.  Gecamines plans to invest US$930B into exploration and modernisation projects in the coming years, aiming at re-establishing itself as a major copper and cobalt producer.  The company was responsible for 18,000t of contained copper output last year but hopes to achieve production of around 100,000t/y contained copper by 2016. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 





- **AO Kazzinc** , a subsidiary of **Glencore International Plc.** , announced on 13<sup>th</sup> September the commissioning of its copper smelting/refining project in Ust-Kamenogorsk, Eastern Kazakhstan. The plant currently has a production capacity of 70,000t, however, there is potential for this figure to rise by a further 17,500t in the future. 

- China’s **Sichuan Hongda** , a major lead and zinc producer, said on 16<sup>th</sup> September that its subsidiary, **Hongda Mo-Cu,** plans to develop a copper smelting/refining project at an investment cost of RMB10.48B (US$1.64B).  The project is set to have a 400,000t/y copper cathode production capacity, and will be developed in two stages, each contributing 200,000t to total smelting and refining capacity.
